_comment: Tracks real, popularity-weighted OSS Terraform/OpenTofu estates run through the five-stage crossing pipeline (cold deploy -> migrate -> test plan -> test apply -> drift and reconverge), same spirit as cohort-acceptance.json but for real-world estates rather than estate-gen's synthetic cohorts. A stage is 'pass', 'fail', or 'not_run' - not_run means the estate's script does not yet exercise that stage, which is itself a gap worth closing, not a silent pass. Updated by the orchestrator from each crossing's own verified run, not by an agent editing this file directly - the same discipline live/cohort-acceptance.json uses, so N concurrent crossings never fight over one JSON file's sort order.

estates.source: hand-written reference project: the plainest getting-started shape (VPC/subnet/SG/IGW/EC2)
estates.notes: Verified end-to-end 2026-08-17/18. Predates the drift-and-reconverge stage being added to the pipeline shape; needs a follow-up pass to add it, same as every other pre-existing corpus-* script.

Landed f6a9f899d0 (2026-08-18), which also fixed a real generalizing bug on the way: live-import's Ratify loop skipped every resource inside a module block (regressed behind closed issue #59's child-module admission, which named five other root-only walkers but never live-import). module.lambda_function.{aws_lambda_function,aws_iam_role,aws_cloudwatch_log_group} now stamp correctly - this affects every real module usage, not just this estate, since virtually all published Terraform modules nest their resources under a module block. test_plan blocked on a separate, still-open gap: two resource blocks (aws_lambda_function_url, aws_lambda_function_recursion_config) use count = var.enable_x ? 1 : 0 with the var false/unset, so stock OpenTofu creates zero instances of either, but choudoufu's type-admission check runs per declared block rather than per resolved instance and refuses the plan outright. A local_file resource is also refused (outside the live-markers subset). Filed as #303. Recommended next slot: a static count-is-zero evaluator feeding type admission - likely high-leverage, since count-gated optional-feature resources are an extremely common module idiom, not specific to this one.

Landed c239792018/47778a931a (2026-08-18); migrate's fail->pass flip was re-verified 2026-08-18 against current main (cec3c4b9b1) but the committed run.sh still asserted the stale pre-fix '0 eligible' shape as a passing control rather than a real check. Follow-up pass 2026-08-18 (this entry) rewrote run.sh's own assertions to the real, current numbers, re-verified for real in a fresh isolated worktree rather than trusted from the prior note: stage 2 dry run reports '23 of 39 resource instance(s) are eligible for stamping (VERIFIED or DRIFTED)' (18 VERIFIED + 5 DRIFTED), -approve reports '23 resource(s) newly stamped, 0 already stamped, 0 failed, 16 skipped', and the primary aws_db_instance's tofu-address/tofu-estate tags are asserted by exact value straight through the AWS CLI (module.db.module.db_instance.aws_db_instance.this:0 / rds-complete-postgres). The 16 skipped: 13 untaggable by design (aws_route_table_association x9, aws_route, aws_security_group_rule, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment, random_id - no tags argument in the provider schema) and 3 are #305's still-open unadmitted-type gap. test_plan is now asserted against a real live-plan on the really-migrated estate (state file deleted first) with a BREAK=1 negative control, and the real counts differ from what the prior note here claimed: exactly 7 count-index-in-tag sites (#304, all aws_security_group_rule.ingress_with_cidr_blocks) and exactly 3 unadmitted-type sites (#305, the three default-object adopters actually created), not 35 and 5. The prior note's 35/5 figures were measured before this estate had ever actually been migrated (nothing tagged, so the 28 module.vpc sibling-indexing sites it also counted never had anything to resolve against) and before bc9ef26638 ('a resource block with a provably-zero count/for_each has no instance to refuse admission on', already on main) landed, which independently stops aws_default_vpc/aws_vpn_gateway_attachment's two count=0 sites from refusing at all - together accounting for the 35->7 and 5->3 drop. Two unrelated real floci gaps found and filed upstream on the fork: lex00/floci#51 (RDS cross-region backup replication), lex00/floci#52 (SecretsManager RotateSecret wrongly requires a Lambda ARN for RDS-managed rotation) - both worked around in the script with documented EMULATOR GAP deltas so stage 1 could stand up at all.

estates.source: terraform-aws-modules/terraform-aws-vpc examples/complete (tag v6.6.1), its flagship example
estates.notes: Landed 9b75cae5ce (2026-08-18). Two real, distinct fixes landed on the way: (1) a floci gap where DescribeVpcEndpointServices always answered empty, blocking every VPC endpoint regardless of service - fixed on the fork (lex00/floci commit 83e44fe6, reconciled into the combined image the orchestrator is republishing) and (2) closed #303 outright (see that issue) via the new generically-derived blockHasNoInstances, hit here through the same terraform-aws-vpc default-object-adoption pattern #305 already named. cold_deploy still fails on floci gaps this crossing judged out of scope for the session rather than sprawling into: Redshift has no service in floci at all (CreateClusterSubnetGroup), plus CreateDhcpOptions, CreateCacheSubnetGroup (ElastiCache) and CreateCustomerGateway/CreateVpnGateway all return UnsupportedOperation with no implementation in floci's Java source. Stages 2-5 are implemented in the script (live-import adoption, empty replan with rendered-identity assertions, no-op apply, drift-and-reconverge on a subnet tag, BREAK=1 controls) but unexercised since stage 1 fails fast by design.

Landed 9717459fd3 (2026-08-18). Crossed by an agent whose worktree, like the original rds-complete-postgres crossing, predates the lambda-simple crossing's live-import child-module fix (cec3c4b9b1) - migrate is recorded fail here ('3 of 4 root-module resources stamped, 50 non-root instances not considered') because that's what the agent's own stale base observed. Given rds-complete-postgres's own re-verification confirmed cec3c4b9b1 generalizes cleanly to a different estate's module-nested resources, this row very likely also improves once re-verified against current main - flagged for the same re-verification treatment, not yet done. test_plan independently fails on unadmitted default_*/VPN-gateway types (overlapping #305's pattern), undeclared-record-store logical resources, and 7 correctly-conservative count-index refusals (element() over a list, which the checker cannot statically prove injective - not a defect). Two real, generalizing floci gaps found and fixed but NOT YET merged/published: EKS worker AMI discovery (AWS-owned AMI catalog lookup, owner 602401143452/801119661308, evaluated unconditionally by every terraform-aws-eks version) and AutoScalingGroup SuspendProcesses/ResumeProcesses (unimplemented, but the AWS provider calls SuspendProcesses unconditionally around ASG creation on default settings - blocks any aws_autoscaling_group apply, not just EKS's). Filed as lex00/floci#55, PR lex00/floci#56, pushed but not merged - the currently-pinned floci image predates both fixes.

Landed 1398574b03 (2026-08-18), 32 instances across 5 module calls. Three real fixes landed on the way: (1) two new admitted types ratified (aws_s3_bucket_accelerate_configuration, _request_payment_configuration - row-gen's own [client-named] proposal, no provider Identity Schema for either), (2) live-import's ratify.go now consults the same schema-based admission fallback internal/live/lint already used at plan time, so it can read sibling types (aws_s3_bucket_acl etc.) a plain live-plan already admitted, and (3) a floci routing bug where PUT /{bucket}?accelerate fell through to bucket creation and 409'd on every apply - fixed on the fork (lex00/floci PR #53, published digest sha256:905c9c67..., not yet merged/reconciled into the combined image). migrate genuinely passes (6 of 32 stamped: the four buckets, IAM role, KMS key; a residue-classification apply in stage 2c left all four bucket markers intact). test_plan blocked by a NEWLY-FOUND, SEVERE defect, filed as #306: choudoufu apply can silently drop a stamped resource's tofu-address/tofu-estate tags from the live object even though the plan shown is correct, for any resource whose own config declares an explicit tags argument (not an edge case - HANDOFF.md ranks a wrong/lost marker above every other defect class). Isolated, minimal repro included in the issue, ruled out floci and the already-fixed #287 item 8 default_tags collision directly. Worked around here by removing the one estate tags block that triggers it; even past that, two more sites (module.s3_bucket's canned acl and website.routing_rules) never converge because their provider Read() needs genuinely-remembered prior state a stateless discovery run can't supply - not attempted, removing acl would desync the estate's own resource count from the honestly cold-deployed original. #306 is now the highest-priority open item this pipeline has surfaced: it undermines the stage-4 no-op-apply guarantee every other crossing in this manifest depends on.
